98 cards. Cover the right column, say the answer aloud, and give an example. To use spaced repetition, import [recall-cards.csv](recall-cards.csv) into Anki or another flashcard app: the columns are front, back, and tags.

## Domain 1 · Ingestion and transformation

| Prompt | Answer to check |
|---|---|
| Kinesis provisioned shard write capacity | 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s per shard, whichever binds first |
| Kinesis shared read bandwidth per shard | 2 MB/s shared by all standard consumers |
| Enhanced fan-out bandwidth | 2 MB/s per shard for each registered consumer |
| Kinesis default and maximum retention | 24 hours by default; up to 365 days |
| Kinesis vs. Firehose vs. MSK | Kinesis: replay and independent consumers. Firehose: managed buffered delivery. MSK: existing Kafka clients |
| What does resharding not fix? | A single hot partition key. All records with that key still go to one shard |
| Stateless vs. stateful processing | Stateless uses only the current record. Stateful keeps information across records, such as a windowed count |
| How does Lambda do simple stateful stream aggregation? | Tumbling windows on a Kinesis or DynamoDB Streams event source mapping |
| Lambda maximum timeout | 900 seconds (15 minutes) |
| Lambda /tmp range | 512 MB default, up to 10,240 MB |
| Reserved vs. provisioned concurrency | Reserved caps and guarantees capacity, protecting downstream systems. Provisioned pre-initializes environments to cut cold starts |
| SQS visibility timeout guidance for Lambda | At least six times the function timeout, plus the batching window |
| How to stop one bad record blocking a Kinesis shard in Lambda | Bisect batch on error, maximum retry attempts or record age, and an on-failure destination |
| Partial batch responses | ReportBatchItemFailures lets Lambda retry only the failed SQS messages or stream records |
| Glue G.1X worker | 1 DPU, 4 vCPU, 16 GB memory |
| Glue Flex execution class | Lower-cost Spark execution for non-urgent jobs that tolerate variable start and finish times |
| Glue ResolveChoice | Settles a column that arrives with mixed types in a DynamicFrame |
| Glue job bookmark reset risk | It can reread earlier inputs while the old output is still there |
| DataSync vs. Transfer Family vs. AppFlow | File share or object store copies; managed SFTP endpoint for partners; SaaS application connectors |
| DMS full load plus CDC | Initial copy plus ongoing change replication from a database that stays online |
| Snowball Edge status | No longer available to new customers. Consider DataSync or Data Transfer Terminals |
| Step Functions vs. MWAA vs. Glue workflows | Serverless state machine with retries; existing Airflow DAGs; Glue jobs and crawlers only |
| Step Functions pattern to wait for a Glue job | The .sync service integration pattern |
| EventBridge Scheduler advantage | Cron schedules in a named time zone |
| EventBridge Pipes | Point-to-point: source, filter, enrich, target, with no custom code |
| Notify on any Glue job failure | EventBridge rule on Glue Job State Change events targeting SNS |
| API returns HTTP 429 | Honor Retry-After, use capped exponential backoff with jitter |
| Write-then-checkpoint | Write the page to a deterministic key first, then save the next token |
| Data API for Redshift | Run SQL over HTTPS with IAM, no drivers or connection pools |
| SAM gradual deployment | AutoPublishAlias plus DeploymentPreference with alarms; CodeDeploy shifts traffic |
| CloudFormation change set vs. drift detection | Preview a planned update vs. find manual changes |

## Domain 2 · Data store management

| Prompt | Answer to check |
|---|---|
| S3 Standard-IA minimums | 30 days, 128 KB billable size |
| Glacier Instant and Flexible minimum duration | 90 days |
| Glacier Deep Archive minimum duration | 180 days |
| Deep Archive retrieval times | Standard within 12 hours, Bulk within 48 hours |
| Glacier Flexible retrieval times | Expedited 1-5 minutes, Standard 3-5 hours, Bulk 5-12 hours |
| Object Lock governance vs. compliance | Governance can be bypassed with special permission. Compliance cannot, even by root |
| Object Lock prerequisite | S3 Versioning |
| S3 Replication Time Control | 99.9% of objects within 15 minutes |
| Replicate objects that existed before the rule | S3 Batch Replication |
| Expiration in a versioned bucket | Adds a delete marker. Add a noncurrent-version action to remove old versions |
| Intelligent-Tiering small objects | Objects under 128 KB are not monitored or auto-tiered |
| DynamoDB per-partition limits | 3,000 read units and 1,000 write units per second |
| DynamoDB maximum item size | 400 KB |
| DynamoDB TTL timing | Typically within a few days; filter expired items in reads |
| GSI vs. LSI | GSI: new partition key, any time. LSI: same partition key, defined at table creation |
| MemoryDB vs. ElastiCache | Durable in-memory primary database vs. cache |
| DocumentDB / Keyspaces / Neptune | MongoDB-compatible / Cassandra-compatible / graph |
| Redshift COPY files that cannot be split | Similar sizes, 1 MB-1 GB compressed, count a multiple of slices |
| Where are COPY row errors? | SYS_LOAD_ERROR_DETAIL |
| Redshift default isolation for new clusters | Snapshot isolation |
| Redshift error 1023 | Serializable isolation conflict; retry or serialize writers with LOCK |
| Spectrum vs. federated query | Spectrum reads S3. Federated query reads RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL or MySQL |
| KEY vs. ALL distribution | KEY co-locates large tables on a join column. ALL copies small, slow-changing tables to every node |
| Redshift Serverless default base capacity | 128 RPUs |
| Athena CTAS/INSERT INTO partition limit | 100 partitions per query |
| Partition projection | Athena computes partition locations from a template; ignores registered partitions |
| MSCK REPAIR TABLE limitation | Works only with Hive-style key=value folders and slows with many partitions |
| EMR and Athena share table definitions | Use the Glue Data Catalog as EMR's Hive metastore |
| Iceberg OPTIMIZE vs. VACUUM | OPTIMIZE compacts files. VACUUM expires snapshots and removes orphan files |
| S3 Tables | Iceberg tables in table buckets with automatic compaction, snapshot management, and file cleanup |
| Partitioning vs. bucketing | Low-cardinality filter column vs. high-cardinality single-value lookups |
| HNSW vs. IVF | HNSW: graph, fast and accurate, more memory. IVF: clusters, faster builds, less memory |
| Bedrock Knowledge Bases default chunking | About 300 tokens, keeping sentences whole |
| DMS Schema Conversion output | Converted schema plus action items for manual conversion |
| SageMaker Catalog lineage vs. ML Lineage Tracking | Data pipeline lineage vs. model training lineage |

## Domain 3 · Operations and support

| Prompt | Answer to check |
|---|---|
| Athena per-query limit vs. workgroup limit | Per-query cancels the query. Workgroup sends an SNS alert |
| CloudWatch Logs default retention | Never expire |
| Subscription filters per log group | 5 |
| Essentials log class limitation | No metric filters, subscription filters, or Live Tail; class fixed at creation |
| One slow Spark task among many fast ones | Data skew. Use AQE skew join or salting |
| Spot belongs on which EMR nodes? | Task nodes |
| IsComplete vs. Completeness | IsComplete: no missing values. Completeness: threshold such as >= 0.95 |
| Stratified sampling | Sample within each group so small groups are represented |
| SPICE vs. direct query | Fast in-memory dashboards vs. always-current data |
| QuickSight name in November 2026 | AWS Quick Sight |
| Who did what to an AWS resource? | CloudTrail management events (90 days in Event history) |
| Who read an S3 object? | CloudTrail data events (off by default) |
| What was the configuration on a past date? | AWS Config configuration history |

## Domain 4 · Security and governance

| Prompt | Answer to check |
|---|---|
| Timeout vs. AccessDenied | Timeout is the network path. AccessDenied is permissions |
| Glue VPC connection security group rule | A self-referencing inbound rule for all TCP ports |
| Partner allowlists one IP for a private Glue job | NAT gateway with an Elastic IP |
| Which services have gateway VPC endpoints? | S3 and DynamoDB only |
| Restrict a bucket to one VPC endpoint | Bucket policy condition aws:SourceVpce |
| CloudTrail Lake status | Closed to new customers May 31 2026; existing customers continue |
| Cross-account KMS decrypt needs | Key policy in the owner account plus IAM policy in the caller account |
| Can another account use the aws/s3 key? | No. Use a customer managed key |
| S3 default encryption since January 2023 | SSE-S3 on all new uploads; cannot be disabled |
| Encrypt before transit | Client-side encryption such as the S3 encryption client or AWS Encryption SDK |
| Require TLS for a bucket | Deny when aws:SecureTransport is false |
| Secrets Manager vs. Parameter Store | Managed rotation vs. low-cost config and SecureString |
| Lake Formation filter levels | Column, row, and cell |
| LF-Tags vs. IAM ABAC | Tag-based catalog grants vs. principal-tag-matches-resource-tag conditions |
| Macie custom data identifier | A regular expression for your own sensitive formats |
| Keep copies in one Region | SCP with aws:RequestedRegion plus restricted replication and Backup copy destinations |
| Domain unit | A business-unit grouping in a Unified Studio domain with delegated policies |
| Subscription fulfillment for Glue assets | Granted automatically through Lake Formation when the table is Lake Formation managed |
